 Southampton star Josh O’Connor misses out on becoming 007

 Southampton 
 By 
 Ross Marshall
 Reporter 
 Share

 Josh O'Connor as Prince Charles in The Crown (Image: Netflix)

 It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.
 Southampton's Josh O’Connor has missed out on becoming the next James Bond after Robert Pattinson was announced as the new 007.
 Pattinson was confirmed as Daniel Craig’s successor on Monday, ending months of speculation over who would take on the iconic role.
 O’Connor had been among the names linked with the part, alongside actors including Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Nicholas Hoult.
 The actor was reportedly offered the role but turned it down, according to reports last week.

 O’Connor had previously played down suggestions he would become the next Bond, describing the prospect of being considered for the role as “extraordinary”.
 Pattinson, 40, will become the seventh actor to play the British spy in an official Bond film.
 The next instalment will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, with Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight writing the screenplay.
 Josh O’Connor has a strong connection to Southampton, having been born in the city in 1990.
